title: Everyday life — the present tense
title_target: আমি রোজ কাজ করি — a-mi roj kaj kô-ri
goal: Talk about daily routines with the present tense, and put the negative না where English speakers never expect it: after the verb.
bekal: form present-tense verbs for আমি, তুমি, আপনি, and সে
make negatives with না, which comes AFTER the verb
describe a day from getting up to going to bed
spot verbs whose vowel rises in the আমি form
use the present for near-future plans, as in “I leave tomorrow”

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — Morning tea on the veranda
dialogs.intro: Seven in the morning. Rahim and Ani sit on the veranda with cups of tea. Watch where the word **না** goes — it never stands in front of the verb the way English “not” does.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Do you get up this early every day?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Yes, I get up at six. Then I go for a walk.
lines.literal: yes, I — six-o'clock-at — get-up. after-that — walk.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Wow! I don't walk in the morning. I just drink tea.
lines.literal: wow! I — morning-in — walk — not. I — only — tea — eat.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.literal: tea — eat? eating — means — surely — eating!

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Ha ha! In Bengali we “eat” tea, “eat” water, even “eat” cigarettes.
lines.literal: ha ha! bengali-in — we — tea — eat, water — eat, cigarette-too — eat.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I see. When do you go to the office?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: I leave at nine. I take the bus, not a rickshaw.
lines.literal: nine-o'clock-at — out — become. bus-by — go, rickshaw-by — go — not.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: She studies. She studies at the university, and in the afternoon she teaches.
lines.literal: she — studies. university-at — studies, and — afternoon-in — teaches.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Do you all eat dinner together?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Yes, every day. Mother cooks, and we all sit down together.
lines.literal: yes, every-day. mother — cooking — does, we — all — sit.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: That's lovely. I don't like eating alone.
lines.literal: very — good — is-feeling. I — alone — to-eat — want — not.

notes: **The negative না comes AFTER the verb, not before it.** This is the exact opposite of English. আমি যাই (I go) → আমি যাই **না** (I don't go). আমি বুঝি (I understand) → আমি বুঝি **না**. ⚠️ The mistake *আমি না যাই* will sound odd at once. A way to remember it: in Bengali **the verb always comes last — unless there is a না, which comes even later.**

**There are only four present-tense endings to learn**, all attached to the same stem: **-ই** for আমি, **-ও** for তুমি, **-এন** for আপনি, **-এ** for সে. করা (to do) → করি · কর · করেন · করে. Once you know these four endings, every Bengali verb opens up — there is no long list of irregular verbs as in English.

⚠️ **Some verbs raise their vowel, and only in the আমি form.** শোনা (to hear) → আমি **শুনি**, but তুমি শোনো, আপনি শোনেন. বোঝা (to understand) → আমি **বুঝি**. লেখা (to write) → আমি **লিখি**. The pattern: **o rises to u, é rises to i**. The other forms stay put. If you forget and say আমি শোনি, people will still understand — but the raised vowel is very characteristic and soon sounds natural.

**খাওয়া means “eat”, and also “drink”, and also “smoke”.** চা খাই = I drink tea. পানি খাই = I drink water. সিগারেট খাই = I smoke. ⚠️ This isn't lazy language but a different way of thinking: Bengali treats everything that goes into the mouth as one action. The word **পান করা** does exist for “drink”, but it sounds formal and is hardly used at home.

**The Bengali present is also used for near-future plans** — much like English “I leave tomorrow”. আমি কাল যাই can mean “I'm going tomorrow”. Bengali uses it more freely than English, but the idea will feel familiar.

**পড়া means to read, and also to study, and also to be a student.** ও পড়ে can mean “she is reading” or “she's at university”. For **teaching**, the word is **পড়ানো** *pôRano* — the same verb plus -আনো, meaning “make someone else do it”. ⚠️ This pattern is very productive: খাওয়া (eat) → খাওয়ানো (feed), দেখা (see) → দেখানো (show), শেখা (learn) → শেখানো (teach).

**Means of transport take the place ending -এ · -তে, not a separate word.** বাসে যাই (go by bus), রিকশায় যাই (go by rickshaw), হেঁটে যাই (go on foot). There is no word for “by” or “take” here — just attach the same ending as “in”. ⚠️ So বাসে means both “in the bus” and “by bus”, and context decides.

grammars.title: The simple present — সাধারণ বর্তমান
after: **The তুই form** (intimate) uses **-ইস**: করিস, যাস, খাস, থাকিস. This module doesn't use it in dialogues, but you'll hear it between close friends and within families.
⚠️ **Verbs never change for plural.** আমি করি and আমরা করি are identical; সে করে and তারা করে are identical. Only the person and the level of respect change.

after: ⚠️ **Three negatives for three jobs — don't mix them up:** **না** negates a verb (this one), **নয়** negates identity with no verb (unit 2), **নেই** negates existence (unit 3). English uses “not” for all three.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Three little words that change a sentence's tone
items: **তো** *to* — “you know”, “after all”. It sits in the middle of a sentence to recall something both sides already know: আপনি তো জানেন (you know that, don't you). Hard to explain, easy to feel — like a spoken tag question.
**তো** also softens requests: একটু দেখুন তো (just take a look, would you). Without তো, the sentence sounds like an order.
**শুধু** *shudhu* — “only, just”. আমি শুধু চা খাই (I only drink tea). And **রোজ** *roj* — “every day”, a word you'll use a lot in this unit.

blocks.text: One note that will save a lot of confusion: everyday Bengali often **drops the subject pronoun** when the verb ending already makes it clear. Since করি can only belong to আমি, people simply say **রোজ কাজ করি** — “work every day”, and everyone knows who is meant. English does this only in casual speech (“Going home?”); Bengali does it all the time. Don't be surprised if what you hear is shorter than what's in the book.

আমি রোজ ছটায় উঠি। — আমি বাসে অফিসে যাই। — আমি বুঝি না। — আম্মা রান্না করেন। — মিতালি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে পড়ে।
